claims.text: Anthropic's long-running harness uses an initializer agent that writes init.sh, claude-progress.txt, an initial commit and a JSON feature list of 200+ features that all initially fail.
Anthropic chose JSON for the feature list because the model is less likely to inappropriately change or overwrite JSON than Markdown.
Anthropic's multi-agent research system uses about 15x more tokens than chat.
Token usage explains 80% of the variance in BrowseComp performance in Anthropic's multi-agent research system.
Anthropic uses rainbow deployments in its multi-agent research system so that in-flight agents are not disrupted during updates.
Anthropic's multi-agent research system resumes agents from checkpoints after errors.
In Anthropic's Managed Agents, the session is an append-only log kept outside both the harness and the sandbox.
In Anthropic's Managed Agents, a crashed harness is replaced by calling wake(sessionId).
Decoupling the harness from the container in Managed Agents cut p50 time-to-first-token by about 60% and p95 by over 90%.
Anthropic removed context resets from its long-running app harness with Opus 4.5.
Anthropic removed the sprint construct from its long-running app harness with Opus 4.6.
Anthropic's full harness run cost $200 over 6 hours, versus a $9, 20-minute solo run whose core feature did not work.
Agent Skills use three-level progressive disclosure: metadata, the SKILL.md body, and linked files.
Anthropic published Agent Skills as an open standard.
